title: Oscar and the Crown
premise: Mara Kavanagh has spent her life in the Valley of the Unnamed, a pocket country erased from every map and sealed against magic, where she serves as royal food-taster to a king who rules nothing but fog. When the old gods resume answering prayers across the valley's borders, the seal begins to crack, and Mara learns her bloodline is the lock: her ancestors traded their names to keep magic out. Hunted by a god who wants its stolen name back and by courtiers who want the valley's last inheritance for themselves, Mara must find the Door Out of a country that no longer exists before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end, she chooses neither escape nor restoration but a third path—giving the name back on her own terms, unsealing the valley and letting her people be remembered, at the cost of her own invisibility forever.
about_author: Sebastian Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing treaties for countries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about borders, bureaucracy, and the people history forgets to mention.

chapters.title: The Taster's Spoon
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She tastes the king's breakfast in a palace that serves no kingdom, establishing the valley's eerie stasis and her careful, invisible life. Emotional beat: quiet pride in being unnoticed.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons on the Kitchen Wall
chapters.summary: Mara notices the kitchen calendar has thirteen moon-marks where twelve should be; the cook insists it has always been so. POV Mara. Beat: first unease, the sense that time itself is miscounting.

chapters.title: A Prayer Overheard
chapters.summary: Oscar, the kitchen boy, whispers a desperate prayer over a dying goat—and something answers. POV Oscar. Beat: wonder curdling into fear as the candle flame bends toward his voice.

chapters.title: The King Who Rules Fog
chapters.summary: Mara is summoned to the throne room; the king is lucid for the first time in years and asks her real name. POV Mara. Beat: terror—names have weight here, and hers was taken at birth.

chapters.title: What the Seal Is Made Of
chapters.summary: The archivist Pell explains the valley's founding bargain: ancestors surrendered their names to bar out magic. POV Pell. Beat: scholarly dread as he shows Mara her own family listed among the nameless.

chapters.title: First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Across the valley, crops heal overnight, a lame girl walks, and old shrines glow. Multiple brief POVs. Beat: communal hope shadowed by the question—who is answering?

chapters.title: The God at the Border Stone
chapters.summary: Oscar sneaks to the border and meets a figure made of antlers and patience who calls him 'little borrower.' POV Oscar. Beat: seduction—the god offers him a name of his own.

chapters.title: Poison, or Prayer
chapters.summary: The king falls ill after tasting nothing harmful; Mara realizes the sickness entered through answered prayers, not food. POV Mara. Beat: guilt—her immunity is useless against this.

chapters.title: The Courtier's Map
chapters.summary: Lady Vess Corvane produces an ancient map showing the Door Out, and quietly recruits allies who want the valley's inheritance. POV Vess. Beat: cold ambition dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Moon the First
chapters.summary: Pell confirms the thirteenth moon is counting down; when it fills, the seal fails entirely. POV Pell. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Immunity
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Mara became a taster, fed poisons since childhood by a mother who wanted her untouchable. POV Mara. Beat: love expressed as harm; belonging through endurance.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Name
chapters.summary: Oscar accepts a small gift from the god—a name whispered only he can hear—and gains small impossible luck. POV Oscar. Beat: intoxication and the first taste of debt.

chapters.title: Vess's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: Vess hosts a dinner where Mara must taste-test while eavesdropping on the conspiracy to reach the Door first. POV Mara. Beat: tension under etiquette.

chapters.title: Shrine Fires
chapters.summary: Villagers who refuse the new gods' gifts find their shrines burned; the valley splits into believers and holdouts. POV new character, the lame girl Wren. Beat: community fracturing.

chapters.title: The King Confesses
chapters.summary: The dying king tells Mara the royal line were the bargainers' jailers, and the crown itself is a key. POV Mara. Beat: inheritance revealed as burden.

chapters.title: Moon the Fourth
chapters.summary: Winter comes early and wrong; the god's influence seeps past border stones. POV Oscar watching his village change. Beat: beauty and wrongness intertwined.

chapters.title: What Pell Burned
chapters.summary: Pell admits he destroyed pages of the founding treaty decades ago—to protect someone. POV Pell. Beat: shame, and a hint the god has been owed a name for generations.

chapters.title: The Door Out
chapters.summary: Mara, Oscar, Pell, and Wren follow Vess's stolen map to a cliff face where a door stands in no wall. POV Mara. Beat: awe—the way out exists, but it is locked with a name.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Trap
chapters.summary: Vess reveals she needed Mara all along: royal blood turns the key. Her mercenaries seize the group. POV Vess. Betrayal beat: she believes she is saving everyone.

chapters.title: The God's Bargain
chapters.summary: At the door, the antlered god appears and offers Mara her true name back if she surrenders the crown-key. POV Mara. Beat: temptation of selfhood versus duty.

chapters.title: Escape Through Fog
chapters.summary: Oscar spends his borrowed name's luck to break them free; the payment ages his hands ten years. POV Oscar. Beat: sacrifice, and grief for what magic costs.

chapters.title: Refuge in the Root Cellars
chapters.summary: The fugitives hide beneath the palace in tunnels older than the valley, finding carvings of the original bargain. POV Wren. Beat: discovery—the ancestors were not victims but volunteers.

chapters.title: Moon the Seventh
chapters.summary: Halfway. The king dies without an heir declared; the crown passes, unstoppably, to the nearest royal blood: Mara. POV Mara. Beat: horror of inheritance arriving unwanted.

chapters.title: Coronation in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Pell crowns Mara in secret among the pots and pans; the cooks kneel. POV Mara. Beat: reluctant belonging—she finally has a place, and it may kill her.

chapters.title: Vess's New God
chapters.summary: Vess, furious, prays for power—and a different, hungrier god answers. POV Vess. Beat: ambition becoming possession.

chapters.title: The Plague of Names
chapters.summary: People across the valley begin forgetting their own names as the thirteenth moon waxes; the god is collecting early. POV Pell documenting the losses. Beat: elegiac dread.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren, healed by the gods' gift, must decide whether to defend the miracle that fixed her leg or the valley that named her. POV Wren. Beat: loyalty tested and chosen.

chapters.title: The Mother's Recipe Book
chapters.summary: Mara finds her late mother's recipe book annotated with antidotes—and one final recipe for 'unbinding.' POV Mara. Beat: posthumous maternal guidance, bittersweet.

chapters.title: Siege of Shrines
chapters.summary: Vess's faction and the believers clash violently at the great shrine; Pell is gravely injured shielding the archives. POV Pell. Beat: the cost of scholarship becomes blood.

chapters.title: Moon the Tenth
chapters.summary: Three moons remain. The border stones crack; fog leaks out and the outside world glimpses the valley for the first time in centuries. POV Oscar. Beat: exposure—invisibility ending whether they choose it or not.

chapters.title: Negotiation with Antlers
chapters.summary: Mara meets the god formally and learns the truth: the stolen name belongs to the land itself, and the valley is its caged body. POV Mara. Beat: moral inversion—the villain is a wounded prisoner.

chapters.title: Vess Ascendant
chapters.summary: Vess, half-consumed by her patron god, takes the palace and declares herself regent, promising to open the Door for everyone—at a price. POV Vess. Beat: tragic conviction.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Recipe
chapters.summary: Mara deciphers her mother's final recipe: unbinding requires a crowned nameless taster willing to swallow the land's name like poison. POV Mara. Beat: resolve forming around terrible terms.

chapters.title: Moon the Twelfth
chapters.summary: Penultimate night. The group makes its separate peace: Oscar renounces magic, Wren rallies the holdouts, Pell dictates his testament. Ensemble POVs. Beat: quiet before the storm.

chapters.title: Storming the Door
chapters.summary: Mara fights through Vess's forces to the cliff door as the thirteenth moon rises full. POV Mara. Beat: kinetic climax, everything wagered.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: At the door, Mara swallows the land's name; Vess's patron god is unmade mid-strike, and Vess collapses, freed and broken. POV alternating Mara/Vess. Beat: climax peak—transformation through self-destruction.

chapters.title: Naming the Valley
chapters.summary: The seal dissolves; the valley re-enters the world with its true name spoken from Mara's mouth, and maps redraw themselves overnight. POV Wren witnessing dawn. Beat: catharsis—belonging achieved by being seen.

chapters.title: The Price of Visibility
chapters.summary: Mara survives but can never again go unnoticed; every eye finds her, every prayer reaches her. She abdicates to a council including Vess, pardoned. POV Mara. Beat: bittersweet cost accounting.

chapters.title: Oscar's Own Name
chapters.summary: With the land freed, the god—now a guardian stag—gives Oscar back more than it took; his hands heal and he chooses to stay as the valley's first ambassador outward. POV Oscar. Beat: earned hope.

chapters.title: The Taster's Last Meal
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Mara cooks a meal for the whole valley, tasting each dish not for poison but for memory, and raises a spoon to the reader. POV Mara. Beat: warm resolution—inheritance transformed into gift.
